+# Declare the getter and signal of a hoisted `<const>` alias

+A handler that calls a `<const>` declared later whose value is another binding holding a function (an alias) compiles to `$a_getter($scope)()`, but no `$a_getter` is declared in either build, so the click throws a `ReferenceError`. The alias's signal is called (`$f2` runs `$a($scope, …)`) but declared only in debug output, where its whole body is `_assert_hoist`; the optimized build drops it and the first render throws a `ReferenceError`. Declare a getter for a hoisted alias (or read it through its alias root), and forward to an alias signal only when it has work in the build being emitted.
+Check: compile `
+# Emit every declaration after the runtime bundle wipes `dist`

+`bundle.mts` removes `packages/runtime-tags/dist` before bundling, but `build:types` (`tsc -b`) keeps its build info in the root `dist/tsconfig.runtime-tags.tsbuildinfo`, so a local `pnpm run build` after an earlier one re-emits only the declarations whose sources changed and leaves the rest of `dist/**/*.d.ts` missing (a fresh CI checkout emits them all). A local pack or a types check against `dist` then reads a partial package. Remove the build info with `dist`, or have `bundle.mts` leave the `.d.ts` files in place.

+Check: `pnpm run build`, touch one runtime source, `pnpm run build` again, then `ls packages/runtime-tags/dist/common` (missing) until `rm dist/tsconfig.runtime-tags.tsbuildinfo && pnpm run build:types`.
+# Keep the read-error stubs out of the optimized html runtime

+`_hoist_read_error`, `_el_read_error` and `_signal_read_error` throw only in debug, but optimized html output references them, so `dist/html.mjs` exports them as empty functions, which `packages/runtime-tags/AGENTS.md` › `MARKO_DEBUG` rules out. Where the stub stands in for a getter that gets called (`((el) => el())(_el_read_error)`, from `visitors/program/html.ts`), it must stay a function; where it is called at the site, its value is `undefined` and optimized output can emit `void 0` instead, as the DOM's hoisted alias read does: `getHTMLReadBase`'s alias branch (`_hoist_read_error()`) and `$signal` on the server (`_signal_read_error()`, `visitors/referenced-identifier.ts`), which is that helper's only site.

+Check: `grep -n "_read_error" packages/runtime-tags/dist/html.mjs` after `pnpm run build`, and `pnpm run compile -- -o html packages/runtime-tags/src/__tests__/fixtures/html-comment-abort-signal/template.marko`.
+# Key the prebuilt test runtime by its build too

+`runtimeSourceKey` hashes the runtime's source files (excluding `__tests__`) and the rolldown version, so an edit to `buildRuntime` itself (its input, defines, plugins) reuses the stale `__tests__/dist/<kind>-<key>` build, and a revert of such a line passes until some runtime file changes. Hash `bundle.ts` into the key as well.

+Check: in a scratch copy with a warm `__tests__/dist`, change `buildRuntime`'s `runtime` input to `path.join(srcDir, `${kind}.ts`)` and run `pnpm test -- --grep "runtime-tags/translator const-tag "`: it passes, and fails once `__tests__/dist` is removed.

- Validate early: core tags share their checks and wording from `util/assert.ts` (`assertOnlyValueAttr`, `assertHasBody`, `assertHasVar`, `assertNoSpreadAttrs`, …), while `assertNoArgs` / `assertNoParams` / `assertNoVar` / `assertAllowedAttributes` come from `@marko/compiler/babel-utils`. Compile errors use `path.buildCodeFrameError` with backticked names and a markojs.com docs link — `util/assert.ts` is the canonical style.

- `util/optional.ts` (`Opt`/`Sorted` list algebra) underpins reference tracking; a list a `Sorted` instance builds (each `new Sorted(…)`) is looked up by binary search, so it is typed `SortedOpt` and only that instance can write it (`push`/`concat` results do not type-check into one). Work on these lists with its helpers (`forEach`, `some`, `reduce`, `filter`, the `Sorted` utils): build-then-`reverse` and dedupe-on-add are smells.

- **`_name` exports** are runtime API called by generated code — public to codegen, not to app authors. Renames must update `callRuntime` call sites and `pureDOMFunctions`. A new helper joins its family's shape (`_<kind>_resume`) and reuses CONTEXT.md's words.

-- **`MARKO_DEBUG`** gates all validation, descriptive names, and detailed error messages (`if (MARKO_DEBUG) { ... }`); builds strip these. Write for the optimized build: debug-only code never leaves it a temporary, `!`, branch or helper, so return directly. Debug differs from production only in names, validation and messages, never in behavior, so a page that works in one build works in the other. Production errors: `throw MARKO_DEBUG ? new Error(msg) : new Error()`. It is `true` for code loaded through the `~ts` register hook; fixture bundles define it per mode (`false` under optimize). Runtime error helpers live in `common/errors.ts`.

A helper only debug output calls is exported from `src/debug/{dom,html}.ts` alone, never `src/dom.ts`/`src/html.ts`, so the optimized runtime has no stub of it and its body needs no `MARKO_DEBUG` check; debug output linked against the optimized runtime then fails on the missing export, a build contract. It is `true` for code loaded through the `~ts` register hook; fixture bundles define it per mode (`false` under optimize). Runtime error helpers live in `common/errors.ts`.

- **`.debug.ts` pairs**: source imports the `.debug` module (e.g. `common/types.ts` imports `./accessor.debug`, which imports `./constants/*.debug`); the production build remaps `X.debug` → `X.ts`. Both files must export identical member names with unique string values. `src/__tests__/debug-pairs.test.ts` checks every pair because the types cannot (each module's `Value` is `typeof import("./<itself>")` and `translator/util/get-accessor-enums.ts` casts `as any`): a member added to one half would type-check and be `undefined` in an optimize build. A runtime record that needs readable debug keys uses a pair, extending the module for the object type that owns the property (repeated short values compress better).
- **Optional feature enablement** (tree-shakable runtime API) has two patterns:

- **`src/{dom,html}/**/*.feat.ts`** are compiler-injected side-effect modules for behavior a referenced import cannot keep alive (catch handling, controllable registration). The build emits them as extra entries of their runtime's bundle — a shared chunk keeps one state instance, so they import runtime internals directly. A feature body only enables: registry/property assignments and installer calls (`installCatch`, `installBranchRenders`) with the callbacks they install; the compiler emits it once per program via `importRuntimeFeature` (typed by `DOMRuntimeFeature`). `lazy.feat` is the exception: `translator/util/entry-builder.ts` › `builder.build` imports it (via `getRuntimeFeatureImport`) into a resuming entry that reaches a lazy import, since resume needs its latch even when no bundled template references lazy runtime. `compat.feat` (dom and html) is the other: it exports the Marko 5 interop API that runtime-class's `tags-compat` entries import, so only Class interop pages load it.
